valuation.method: Forward adjusted EPS x P/E on FY2027 EPS (year priced at the 2027-11-18 target date). Anchors: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $14.08 (record, realized refining margin $38/bbl vs $24.08 in Q2), 9M 2026 adjusted EPS $23.89, Q3 diluted shares about 399 million with $2.27bn buybacks in the quarter. FY2027 EPS values are our assumptions of how far record cracks normalize; multiples are low-to-mid cycle refiner multiples applied to elevated earnings, not broker targets. US common share in USD, so no ADR or FX conversion.

bear.driver: Crack spreads revert most of the way to mid-cycle and chemicals/marketing stay weak

base.driver: Margins fade from Q3 record but stay well above 2025 levels, 95%+ utilization, steady buybacks

bull.driver: Tight product markets persist through 2027 with buybacks shrinking the share count

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY2027 EPS of $24 the close of $264.90 implies 11.0x; on 9M 2026 adjusted EPS annualized (about $31.9) it is 8.3x. The highest named target ($346, Wells Fargo) implies 14.4x base EPS or EPS near $31.5 at 11x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $24 (9.1% of the close, 9.1 pp). A $1 change in FY2027 EPS at 11x moves it by $11 (4.2 pp).
valuation.watch_metric: Realized refining margin per barrel and Gulf Coast/US crack spreads versus the $38/bbl Q3 record.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 and full-year 2026 results, expected around late January or early February 2027 (date not retrieved).

analyst_notes: Named targets jumped after the Q3 record: Wells Fargo $346, TD Cowen $308, Mizuho $300 (while downgrading to Neutral), UBS $300 and Goldman $274 versus $200-235 in summer. Most post-Q3 targets sit above our $264 base (up to 31% above), which needs about $31 EPS at 11x versus our $24. Piper Sandler's $209 (August) is stale; target horizons are not documented so none enter the weighted target.
